Rashi on Shabbat 40b:10:1.english: One may not rinse - Lest one come to level depressions.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:11:1.hebrew: דהא מעשה דרבי אחר גזירה הוה - שגזרו על הזיעה, ועל כרחין בחמי טבריא הוא דהוי. ורבי יהושע דאמר לעיל — בימי רבי הוה, אלמא בימי רבי כבר נגזרה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:11:1.english: As the incident with Rabbi was after the decree - [Namely, the decree in] which they decreed against sweating, and perforce it was in the hot springs of Tiberias that [the incident] occurred. And Rabbi Yehoshua, who stated [the decrees] above, was in the days of Rabbi; evidently, by the days of Rabbi [it] had already been decreed.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:11:2.hebrew: וקאמר ליה טול בכלי שני - אבל ראשון לא, אלמא יש בהן משום בישול:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:11:2.english: And he said to him: “Take in a secondary vessel” - But [in] a primary vessel, no; evidently, there is [a prohibition of] cooking in them.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:2.english: That he was floating in a bath - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:3.hebrew: ולא ידענא אי עקר - רגליו מן הארץ, דקסבר: כי תנן "אין שטין על פני המים" במשילין פירות — בנהר גדול תנן, דאיכא למגזר שמא יעשה חבית של שייטין, כדאמרינן התם; אבל באמבטי — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:3.english: And I do not know if he lifted - His feet from the ground. For he held: When we learned [in the Mishnah], "One may not swim upon the water," in the chapter [entitled] Mashilin Peirot, we learned [this only] regarding a large river, where there is [reason] to decree lest one make a swimmer's float, as we say there; but in a bathtub, no.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:4.english: [Or] if he did not lift - His feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:5.hebrew: לא ישוט - דאע"ג דליכא למיגזר, אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:5.english: [A person] may not float - For even though there is no [reason] to decree, it is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:12:6.english: And even if it stands in a courtyard - Where there is no [reason] to decree lest he splash water with his feet beyond four cubits.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:1:1.hebrew: כי האי תנא - דאמר לעיל: "משהתחילו עוברי עבירה התחילו לאסור הזיעה". והרי לא נאסרה אלא ע"י הרוחצין בחמין מאתמול ואומרים "מזיעין אנחנו", ואין כאן אלא עבירת דבריהם, שאסרו את החמין:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:1:1.english: According to this tanna - Who said above: "Once transgressors began, they began to prohibit sweating." And behold, it was prohibited only on account of those who would bathe in hot water [heated] from yesterday and say, "We are sweating," and there is only here a violation of their [the Sages'] words, who prohibited hot water.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:2:1.english: Their heat is great - And [one] sweats.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:1.english: He warms - He heats [it]; an expression of poshrin [lukewarm water].

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:3.hebrew: אלונטית - טיול"א. ונראה לי: בגד שמסתפגין בו, דבכל דוכתא קרי לה אלונטית:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:3.english: A towel [aluntit] - tewale [towel]. And it seems to me [that it is] a cloth with which one dries oneself, for everywhere [the Gemara] calls that an aluntit.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:4.hebrew: על גבי מעיים - כשהוא חש במעיו, מחממין לו כלי או בגד ומניחו שם, ומועיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:4.english: On the intestines - When one feels pain in his intestines, they heat a vessel or a cloth for him and place it there, and it is beneficial.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:5.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יביא קומקומוס כו' - שמא ישפכו עליו, ונמצא רוחץ בשבת בחמין:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:5.english: As long as one does not bring a kettle, etc. - Lest [the water] spill on him, and he will turn out to be washing with hot water on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:3:6.english: Due to danger - Sometimes [the water] is boiling.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:1.english: Not that they will heat up - Not that he may leave them there until they heat up.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:2.hebrew: אלא שתפיג צינתן - במקצתן. שתפיג — שתתחלף, כמו "וריחו לא נמר" (ירמיהו מ״ח:י״א), מתרגמין: "וריחיה לא פג":
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:2.english: Rather, so that their chill will dissipate - [Only] partially. “That it will dissipate” — that it will change, as [in the verse]: “And his scent was not changed” (Jeremiah 48:11), which is translated: “And his scent did not dissipate.”

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:3.hebrew: לא בשביל שיבשל - שלא תניחנו שם כדי בישול, שתהא היד סולדת בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:3.english: Not so that it will cook - That she should not leave it there to the point of cooking, such that the hand recoils from it:

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:4.hebrew: סכה ידה - אבל להפשירו בפך כדרך שעושה בחול — לא; ופליג אדרב יהודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:4:4.english: Smears her hand - But to warm it in a cruse in the manner that she does on a weekday — [she may] not; and he disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:1.hebrew: להתירא - מאי דאסר רבי יהודה בשמן — בישול — שרי ת"ק. ומים דוקא נקט "ולא שיחמו", דיש בהן בישול; אבל שמן, אע"פ שהיד סולדת — דהיינו בישול דר' יהודה — שרי לת"ק:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:1.english: To permit - That which Rabbi Yehuda prohibited regarding oil — [namely,] cooking — the first tanna permits. And he specifically stated “and not that they heat up” regarding water, as it is subject to cooking; but oil, even though the hand recoils from it — which is [what constitutes] cooking according to Rabbi Yehuda — is permitted according to the first tanna.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:2.hebrew: סולדת - נמשכת לאחוריה מדאגה שלא תכוה. וזהו לשון "ואסלדה בחילה" (איוב ו׳:י׳) — ואדאג ברעדה, ואמשך מתלונתי מדאגת יום הדין, אם הייתי יודע שמיתתי קרובה ולא יחמול:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:2.english: Recoils - [The hand] draws backward out of fear that it will be burned. And this is [the same as] the expression: “And I would recoil in anguish” (Job 6:10) — [meaning,] I would worry in trembling, and withdraw from my complaint out of fear of the Day of Judgment, if I knew that my death was near and [that] He would not spare [me].

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:3.hebrew: שמן יש בו משום בישול - הלכך, לא כדי שיבשל, אלא כדי שיפשר שרי, דהפשרו אין זה בישולו:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:3.english: Oil is subject to [the prohibition of] cooking - Therefore, [placing it] not so that it will cook, but rather so that it will warm, is permitted, for warming it is not [tantamount to] cooking it.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:4.hebrew: ואתא רבי שמעון למימר דהפשירו זהו בישולו - הלכך, כדעבדין בחול לא ליעביד, אלא כלאחר יד, על ידי שינוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:5:4.english: And Rabbi Shimon came to say that warming it is [tantamount to] cooking it - Therefore, one should not do as one does on a weekday, but rather in a backhanded manner, by means of an alteration.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:6:1.hebrew: לאיסורא - אמרה תנא קמא לשמן: דמיא הוא דשרי להפשיר, אבל שמן — הפשרו זהו בישולו:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:6:1.english: To prohibit - The first tanna stated [this] with regard to oil: that it is [only] water that is permitted to be warmed, but [as for] oil, warming it is its cooking.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:6:2.hebrew: איכא בינייהו כלאחר יד - דלתנא קמא, אפי' ע"י שינוי אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:6:2.english: There is [a difference] between them [regarding doing so] in a backhanded manner - For according to the first tanna, [it is] forbidden even by means of a variation.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:7:1.hebrew: והיכי דמי - סלוד? יש שסולד מרתיחה מועטת, ויש שאינו סולד:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:7:1.english: And what are the circumstances - [Of] recoiling? There is [one] who recoils from slight heat, and there is [one] who does not recoil.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:1.hebrew: נכנסתי - בשבת; ובחמי טבריא הוה, שלא נאסרו, כדאמר לעיל: "התירו להם חמי טבריא":
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:1.english: I entered - [This occurred] on Shabbat; and it was in the hot springs of Tiberias, which were not forbidden, as [the Gemara] said above: “They permitted the hot springs of Tiberias to them.”

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:2.hebrew: באמבטי - כגון בריכה עשויה בקרקע, שהמים נכנסים שם ונאספין:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:2.english: In a bathtub - Such as a pool made in the ground, into which the water enters and collects.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:3.hebrew: ובקשתי להניח שם פך שמן - להפשיר, לסוך הימנו קודם הרחיצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:3.english: And I sought to place a jar of oil there - To warm [it], [in order] to anoint with it before bathing.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:5.hebrew: בכלי שני - שיצטננו מעט, דכלי שני אינו מבשל, ואח"כ תן הפך לתוך אותו כלי שני. דהך אמבטי, שהחמין נמשכין לה מן המעיין, חשיב לה ככלי ראשון שנרתחו בו, שאע"פ שהעבירו מעל האור מבשל, כדתנן לקמן (שבת ד' מב.): "האילפס והקדירה שהעבירן מרותחין, לא יתן לתוכן תבלין":
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:5.english: In a secondary vessel - So that [the water] will cool down slightly, for a secondary vessel does not cook, and afterwards place the jar into that secondary vessel. For he considered this bathtub, into which hot water is drawn from the spring, like a primary vessel in which [water] was boiled, which cooks even though one removed it from the fire, as we learned below (Shabbat 42a): "A stew pot and a pot that one removed [while] boiling, one may not place spices into them."

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:6.hebrew: וש"מ הפשרו - במקום הראוי לבישול:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:6.english: And learn from it [that] warming it - [That is,] in a place capable of cooking.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:7.hebrew: זהו בישולו - דהא להפשיר בעלמא הוא דקבעי, ואסר ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:8:7.english: Is its cooking - For he only sought to warm [it], yet [Rabbi] forbade him [to do so].

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:9:1.hebrew: והיכי עביד הכי - להורות הוראה, שהוא דבר תורה, בבית המרחץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:9:1.english: And how could he do this? - To issue a ruling, which is a matter of Torah, in the bathhouse:

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:9:2.english: To contemplate - On words of Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 40b:9:4.hebrew: אסור לאומרן - במקום הטנופת, ואפי' בלשון חול:
Rashi on Shabbat 40b:9:4.english: [It is] forbidden to say them - In a filthy place, and even in a secular language.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:3:1.hebrew: מפני שמפשיר מים שעליו - בכולה שמעתא ובמתניתין גבי מיחם שפינהו משמע, דלהפשיר מים לצורך שתייה מותר — דהפשירן לא זהו בישולן. והכא דאסורין — מפרש ריב"א דדומה כרוחץ במים חמין, ויבא להחם חמין לרחוץ גופו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:3:1.english: Because he warms the water on him - Throughout the entire sugya and in the Mishnah regarding “a kettle that one emptied,” it is implied that warming water for drinking is permitted, as warming them [to lukewarm] is not [considered] cooking them. And here, where [it] is forbidden, the Riva explains that it resembles washing in hot water, and one might come to heat hot water to wash his body.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:3:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יביא קומקומוס כו' - פירוש: כל זמן שהאלונטית שם, שמא יפלו המים על האלונטית ואתי לידי סחיטה. אי נמי: לא יביא משום רפואה, וגזרו אטו שחיקת סממנים טפי מבאלונטית, דלא מיחזי כרפואה כ"כ:
Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:3:2.english: "Provided that he does not bring a kettle, etc." - Explanation: [This applies] as long as the towel is there, lest the water fall onto the towel and he come to wring [it] out. Alternatively: He may not bring [it] because of healing, and they decreed [against this] due to [the concern of] grinding herbs, more so than with a towel, which does not appear so much like healing.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:8:1.hebrew: ושמע מינה כלי שני אינו מבשל - תימה: מאי שנא כלי שני מכלי ראשון? דאי יד סולדת — אפי' כלי שני נמי, ואי אין יד סולדת — אפילו כלי ראשון נמי אינו מבשל! ויש לומר: לפי שכלי ראשון, מתוך שעמד על האור, דופנותיו חמין ומחזיק חומו זמן מרובה, ולכך נתנו בו שיעור דכל זמן שהיד סולדת בו אסור; אבל כלי שני, אף על גב דיד סולדת בו מותר, שאין דופנותיו חמין והולך ומתקרר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:8:1.english: "And learn from this that a secondary vessel does not cook" - It is astonishing: In what way is a secondary vessel different from a primary vessel? For if the hand recoils from it, even a secondary vessel too should cook, and if the hand does not recoil from it, even a primary vessel too does not cook! And one can say: Because with a primary vessel, since it stood upon the fire, its walls are hot and it retains its heat for a long time, and therefore they established a measure for it that as long as the hand recoils from it, cooking in it is forbidden. However, with a secondary vessel, even though the hand recoils from it, placing food into it is permitted, for its walls are not hot and it steadily cools down.

Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:9:1.hebrew: וכי תימא בלשון חול קאמר ליה - ואע"ג דאסור להרהר, נימא דאין אסור להרהר אלא בלשון קדש, והוא הרהר בלשון חול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 40b:9:1.english: "And if you say that he spoke to him in a secular language" - And even though it is forbidden to contemplate [Torah in a bathhouse], we might say that it is forbidden to contemplate only in the sacred language, and he contemplated in a secular language.
